text:
Sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog rankings; the 2025 study [On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) distinguishes resolution, fidelity, robustness, and predictive power. [Improved Estimation of Ranks (2024)](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/) shows benefits from correcting sampled rank estimates. Implication for this benchmark: retain pinned macro validation HR@10 for selection; use repeated, shared negative sets to diagnose model-order reversals and hit-rate variability, with full-catalog validation ranking as a separate diagnostic where affordable.

Representation evidence supports spectral diagnostics: [Guo et al., ICML 2024](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html) document embedding collapse, while [spectral popularity analysis (2024–2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12008) connects dimensional collapse with amplification of popularity-dominated score components. Effective rank is exp(−Σpᵢ log pᵢ), with pᵢ = σᵢ/Σσⱼ ([original definition](https://www.eurasip.org/Proceedings/Eusipco/Eusipco2007/Papers/a5p-h05.pdf)). Proposed probes: exclude padding; measure item-embedding and sequence-feature spectra; report centering and normalization explicitly; stratify validation hits, misses, and recommendation exposure by training-item frequency. Low effective rank alone does not establish poor ranking or identify its cause.

For uncertainty, a proposed analysis is paired user bootstrap within each category, recomputing the equal-weight four-category macro score and model differences. Keep candidate-resampling variability separate from user-sampling uncertainty. Test whether probes predict validation gains across trials and categories before using them to guide changes. Tail-specific errors motivate sampling experiments; spectral concentration motivates representation experiments; unstable rankings motivate stronger evidence before selection. These are diagnostic hypotheses, not established predictors of this task’s HR@10; no task-specific predictive evidence was found.
